title: Module 3 · Lesson 3 — Prompting vs. RAG vs. fine-tuning

lines: Module Three, Lesson Three: prompting, RAG, or fine-tuning.
It's the exam's most frequent decision question.

say.0: Module Three, Lesson Three: prompting, rag, or fine-tuning.

lines: Picture a bank's support assistant that quotes last week's savings rates and ignores the required reply format.
The team's instinct is to fine-tune on everything.
But the rule is: RAG for knowledge, fine-tuning for behavior.
Prompting covers everything you can get away with.

say.0: But the rule is: rag for knowledge, fine-tuning for behavior.

lines: Use RAG when facts change, answers need citations, or access varies by user.
Knowledge can be added or revoked instantly, with no retraining.

say.0: Use rag when facts change, answers need citations, or access varies by user.

lines: Use fine-tuning for a consistent format, tone, or tool-call syntax.
It can even make a small model match a big one on a narrow task.
So the bank retrieves live rates, and fine-tunes a small model for its format.
Together they give large-model quality at small-model cost.
Full fine-tuning updates every weight, and costs the most.
LoRA trains just a tenth of a percent to one percent of them.

say.1: Lora trains just a tenth of a percent to one percent of them.

lines: LoRA freezes the base weights, so one deployed model can serve many adapters.
NIM supports this: a custom variant per customer, on a tight GPU budget.

say.0: Lora freezes the base weights, so one deployed model can serve many adapters.
say.1: Nim supports this: a custom variant per customer, on a tight G P U budget.

lines: DPO learns from chosen and rejected pairs, and RFT from a verifier, like passing tests.
Distillation shrinks a large model's behavior into a small one.

say.0: D P O learns from chosen and rejected pairs, and R F T from a verifier, like passing tests.

lines: Data quality beats quantity.
A thousand clean examples routinely beat a hundred thousand scraped ones, which is why NeMo Curator exists.

say.1: A thousand clean examples routinely beat a hundred thousand scraped ones, which is why Neemo Curator exists.

lines: Beware catastrophic forgetting, where narrow fine-tuning breaks unrelated skills.
Prefer LoRA, mix in general data, and evaluate on a broad held-out suite.

say.1: Prefer lora, mix in general data, and evaluate on a broad held-out suite.

lines: NVIDIA's data flywheel loops through capture, curate, customize, evaluate, and deploy.
The payoff is a small model, tuned on real traffic, matching a big one at a fraction of the cost.

say.0: En-vidia's data flywheel loops through capture, curate, customize, evaluate, and deploy.

lines: The classic trap: a bot quotes outdated prices, so should you fine-tune on the new price list?
No: fine-tuning teaches how to answer, while retrieval supplies what's true right now.
That one rule wins the exam's most common question.
Read on for the full decision table and every tuning method.
